text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System said Tuesday it was evaluating its position on Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp, the embattled hospital giant in which CalPERS holds a large stake.

"We do own a stake. We have about 3.7 million shares. We're currently evaluating our position right now," said Brad Pacheco, spokesman for CalPERS, the largest public pension system in the United States.
"We have no plans at this point, but we'd like to take a look at some of these other lawsuits," Pacheco said.

State pension systems for New York, Florida and Louisiana have filed lawsuits against Nashville, Tenn.-based Columbia, the focus of a massive federal probe into possible Medicare fraud and other possible wrongdoing.
A spokesman for the New York State Comptroller's office said it has been named lead plaintiff in a consolidated suit including Florida and Louisiana.
"We are, in fact, the lead plaintiff in the consolidated suit and we are filing along with Louisiana and Florida," said the spokesman in Albany, N.Y.
Shares in Columbia were off 7/16 at 33-3/16.
The company has more than 600 million common shares outstanding. It is the largest for-profit hospital company in the United States.
